questions.q: Where should a capital letter go: my friend ana is here.
options: At the start and on Ana
questions.explain: The first word of a sentence and a person's name both get capital letters.

rounds.title: Punctuation for Kids
rounds.desc: Learn when to use a period, question mark, exclamation point, capital letter, and comma.

title: Short Stories
subject: Kids Reading
description: Read a very short story and answer who, where, and what happened.

questions.q: Read: Ana found a lost puppy by the gate. She gave it water and called its owner. Who found the puppy?
questions.explain: The story says Ana found the puppy by the gate.

questions.q: Read: Ana found a lost puppy by the gate. She gave it water and called its owner. What did Ana give the puppy first?
questions.explain: Ana gave the puppy water before she called its owner.

questions.q: Read: Tom planted seeds in a cup. He watered them each day. Soon green leaves grew. What grew?
questions.explain: The story says green leaves grew after Tom watered the seeds.

questions.q: Read: Tom planted seeds in a cup. He watered them each day. Soon green leaves grew. Why did the leaves grow?
options: Tom watered the seeds each day
questions.explain: Tom watered the seeds each day, which helped them grow.

questions.q: Read: Mia rode her bike to the library. She picked a book about whales. Where did Mia go?
questions.explain: Mia rode her bike to the library.

questions.q: Read: Mia rode her bike to the library. She picked a book about whales. What was her book about?
questions.explain: She picked a book about whales.

questions.q: Read: Ben lost his red cap at the park. His sister found it under a bench. Where was the cap?
questions.explain: His sister found the cap under a bench.

questions.q: Read: Lily made soup with her grandma. They added carrots and beans. Then they ate it together. Who cooked with Lily?
questions.explain: Lily made soup with her grandma.

questions.q: Read: A turtle walked slowly to the pond. A rabbit ran past, then stopped to nap. The turtle kept walking and reached the pond first. Who reached the pond first?
questions.explain: The turtle kept walking while the rabbit napped, so the turtle arrived first.

questions.q: Read: Sam heard a noise in the box. He opened it slowly. Inside was a tiny kitten. How did Sam open the box?
questions.explain: The story says he opened it slowly.

rounds.title: Short Stories
rounds.desc: Read a very short story and answer who, where, and what happened.

title: Story Sequencing
subject: Kids Reading
description: Put story events in order using first, next, then, and last, and use clues to tell what happens next.

questions.q: Which word tells what happens at the very beginning of a story?
questions.explain: First tells the beginning event in a sequence.

questions.q: Put in order: He ate the sandwich. He made the sandwich. He bought bread. What happened first?
questions.explain: You must buy the bread before you can make and eat the sandwich.

questions.q: Read: First, Zoe put on socks. Next, she put on shoes. Last, she tied the laces. What did Zoe do last?
questions.explain: Last tells the final step: she tied the laces.

questions.q: Which sentence uses a sequence word correctly?
options: Then, we washed our hands before lunch.
questions.explain: Then is a sequence word that shows order: Then, we washed our hands.

questions.q: Read: A seed is planted. A sprout pops up. A flower opens. What happens just before the flower opens?
questions.explain: The sprout pops up right before the flower opens.

questions.q: If a story says 'Finally, the bus arrived,' the bus arriving is probably:
options: Near the end of the story
questions.explain: Finally signals an event near the end.

questions.q: Read: Max missed the bus, so he walked. Because he walked, he was late. Why was Max late?
options: He missed the bus and walked
questions.explain: Missing the bus and walking caused Max to be late.

questions.q: Which order makes sense for getting ready for bed?
options: Get in bed, brush teeth standing outside, wake up
Brush teeth, put on pajamas, get in bed
Wake up, get in bed, brush teeth
Put on pajamas, wake up, get in bed
questions.explain: A sensible bedtime order is brush teeth, put on pajamas, then get in bed (pajamas first is also sensible, but this is the only fully sensible order listed).

questions.q: Read: The rain filled the puddle. A paper boat floated on it. What will most likely happen if it rains more?
options: The boat will sink at once
questions.explain: More rain adds more water, so the puddle will most likely get bigger.

questions.q: A story ends: '...and from that day on, Pip never forgot his umbrella.' This ending tells you Pip learned to:
questions.explain: The ending says Pip never forgot his umbrella again - he learned to remember it.

rounds.title: Story Sequencing
rounds.desc: Put story events in order using first, next, then, and last, and use clues to tell what happens next.

title: Chapter Book Comprehension
subject: Kids Reading
description: Read a short chapter-book style passage and find details, feelings, lessons, and word meanings in context.

questions.q: Read: Chapter 1. Nora moved to a new town. On her first day, she sat alone at lunch until a girl named Priya shared her orange and asked about Nora's old school. How did Nora most likely feel at first?
questions.explain: Sitting alone in a new town suggests Nora felt lonely at first.

questions.q: Read the same passage about Nora and Priya. What kind thing did Priya do?
options: She shared her orange and talked with Nora
questions.explain: Priya shared her orange and asked about Nora's old school.

questions.q: Read: Jake practiced free throws every afternoon. In the big game he missed his first two shots, took a deep breath, and made the third. What lesson fits best?
options: Winning is the only thing that matters
questions.explain: Jake kept trying after missing and then succeeded, showing persistence.

questions.q: Read: 'The cave was pitch black, so Ben held his flashlight steady.' What does pitch black mean here?
questions.explain: In context, pitch black means completely dark, which is why Ben needed a flashlight.

questions.q: Read: Rosa found a map in her grandfather's attic. The map showed an X near the old oak tree. Rosa grabbed a small shovel. What will Rosa most likely do next?
options: Dig near the old oak tree
Read the map to her class only
questions.explain: The X on the map and the shovel suggest Rosa will dig near the old oak tree.

questions.q: Read: 'Sam was thrilled when his science project won a ribbon.' Which word is a clue that thrilled means very happy?
options: won a ribbon - a happy event
questions.explain: Winning a ribbon is a happy event, which clues you that thrilled means very happy.

questions.q: Read: Chapter 3. The bridge was broken, so the team built a raft from logs. They floated across one by one. What problem did the team solve?
options: How to cross where the bridge was broken
questions.explain: The broken bridge was the problem; the raft was their solution for crossing.

questions.q: Read: Emma promised to return the library book on Friday. On Friday she left it at home, so on Monday she apologized and paid the late fee. What does this show about Emma?
options: She did not care about the book
She took responsibility for her mistake
questions.explain: Apologizing and paying the fee shows Emma took responsibility.

questions.q: Read: 'The wind howled all night, and the windows rattled.' The author uses these details mainly to make the night feel:
questions.explain: Howling wind and rattling windows create a scary, stormy feeling.

questions.q: Read: Leo read three books about sharks. Then he gave a talk to his class about how sharks help the ocean. What is the main idea?
options: Leo learned about sharks and shared what he learned
questions.explain: The main idea covers both parts: Leo learned about sharks and shared that learning.

rounds.title: Chapter Book Comprehension
rounds.desc: Read a short chapter-book style passage and find details, feelings, lessons, and word meanings in context.

title: Maps, Globes and the Compass
subject: Kids Geography
description: Learn to read a simple map, use a compass rose, and find places on a globe with north, south, east, and west.

questions.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
questions.explain: Most maps put north at the top. The compass rose on a map shows you all the main directions.

questions.q: What tool on a map shows the directions north, south, east, and west?
questions.explain: A compass rose is a star-like symbol with arrows pointing in each direction. It helps you figure out which way places are from each other.

questions.q: If you face north, which direction is behind you?
questions.explain: North and south are opposites. If north is in front of you, south is right behind you.

questions.q: The sun rises in which direction?
questions.explain: The sun comes up in the east every morning. It sets in the west at the end of the day.

questions.q: What is a globe?
options: A flat drawing of one city
A round model of the Earth
questions.explain: A globe is shaped like a ball, just like the real Earth. It shows continents and oceans in their true shapes.

questions.q: On a map, what does a map key (or legend) tell you?
options: What the symbols on the map mean
questions.explain: A map key explains the pictures and colors on a map, like a blue line for a river. Always check the key when you see a new symbol.

questions.q: If a town is to the right of your town on a normal map, which direction is it?
questions.explain: On a normal map with north at the top, the right side is east. The left side is west.

questions.q: What does a map scale help you figure out?
options: How far apart places really are
questions.explain: A scale shows how a short distance on the map matches a long distance in real life, like one inch standing for ten miles.

questions.q: Which direction is halfway between north and east on a compass rose?
questions.explain: In-between directions combine two main directions. Northeast sits between north and east on the compass rose.

questions.q: You walk toward the sunset in the evening. Which direction are you walking?
questions.explain: The sun sets in the west, so walking toward the sunset means walking west. Morning walkers facing the sunrise face east.

rounds.title: Maps, Globes and the Compass
rounds.desc: Learn to read a simple map, use a compass rose, and find places on a globe with north, south, east, and west.

description: The 7 continents, the 5 oceans, and where to find famous animals and places.

questions.explain: Earth has 7 continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America.
questions.q: How many continents are there on Earth?

questions.explain: The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean. It is bigger than all the land on Earth put together!
questions.q: Which is the biggest ocean on Earth?

questions.explain: Kangaroos live in the wild in Australia.
questions.q: On which continent do kangaroos live in the wild?

questions.explain: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, France, which is in Europe.
questions.q: On which continent is the Eiffel Tower?

questions.explain: The Arctic Ocean is at the top of the world, around the North Pole.
questions.q: Which ocean is at the top of the world, around the North Pole?

questions.explain: Many penguins live in Antarctica, the cold continent at the South Pole.
questions.q: On which continent do many penguins live, near the South Pole?

questions.explain: The United States is in North America, along with Canada and Mexico.
questions.q: Which continent is the United States on?

questions.explain: The Atlantic Ocean sits between America on one side and Europe and Africa on the other.
questions.q: Which ocean is between America and Europe?

questions.explain: Lions and elephants live in the wild in Africa.
questions.q: On which continent do lions and elephants roam in the wild?

questions.explain: Asia is the largest continent. More people live there than anywhere else!
questions.q: Which is the largest continent?

subject: Kids Geography
title: Continents & Oceans
Hemispheres and the Equator
subject: Kids Geography
description: Discover the imaginary lines that split Earth into halves: the equator, the hemispheres, and the North and South Poles.

questions.q: What is the equator?
options: A real rope tied around the Earth
The line at the top of a map
An imaginary line around the middle of the Earth
questions.explain: The equator is an imaginary line that circles Earth halfway between the poles. Places near it are warm all year.

questions.q: The equator splits the Earth into which two halves?
questions.explain: Hemisphere means half of a sphere. The equator gives us a top half and a bottom half of the Earth.

questions.q: Is the United States above or below the equator?
options: Below it, in the Southern Hemisphere
Above it, in the Northern Hemisphere
questions.explain: The United States sits above the equator in the Northern Hemisphere. That is why its summer is in June, July, and August.

questions.q: Where is the North Pole?
options: At the very bottom of the Earth
At the very top of the Earth
In the middle of the Pacific Ocean
questions.explain: The North Pole is the northernmost point on Earth. It is covered in ice and is where Santa is said to live in stories.

questions.q: Which animal lives near the South Pole but not the North Pole?
questions.explain: Penguins live in the south, around Antarctica near the South Pole. Polar bears live in the north, so the two never meet in the wild.

questions.q: When it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere, what season is it in the Southern Hemisphere?
questions.explain: The two hemispheres have opposite seasons. When the north tilts toward the sun, the south tilts away and has winter.

questions.q: Australia is in which hemisphere for north and south?
questions.explain: Australia lies below the equator, so it is in the Southern Hemisphere. Its Christmas happens during its summer.

questions.q: What are the lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole called?
questions.explain: Longitude lines run pole to pole like the slices of an orange. Latitude lines run sideways around the Earth.

questions.q: Places close to the equator are usually:
questions.explain: The sun shines most directly at the equator, making it hot. Rainforests grow in many warm places near the equator.

questions.q: The Prime Meridian is a special longitude line that passes through which city?
questions.explain: The Prime Meridian is longitude zero and passes through Greenwich in London. Longitude is counted east and west from this line.

rounds.title: Hemispheres and the Equator
rounds.desc: Discover the imaginary lines that split Earth into halves: the equator, the hemispheres, and the North and South Poles.

description: Match famous US states with their capital cities.

questions.explain: Sacramento is the capital of California. Los Angeles is a bigger city, but it is not the capital.
questions.q: What is the capital of California?

questions.explain: Austin is the capital of Texas.
questions.q: What is the capital of Texas?

questions.explain: Tallahassee is the capital of Florida.
questions.q: What is the capital of Florida?

questions.explain: Albany is the capital of New York state, not New York City.
questions.q: What is the capital of New York?

questions.explain: Phoenix is the capital of Arizona.
questions.q: What is the capital of Arizona?

questions.explain: Olympia is the capital of Washington state. Seattle is bigger, but it is not the capital.
questions.q: What is the capital of Washington?

questions.explain: Denver is the capital of Colorado.
questions.q: What is the capital of Colorado?

questions.explain: Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii.
questions.q: What is the capital of Hawaii?

questions.explain: Salem is the capital of Oregon.
questions.q: What is the capital of Oregon?

questions.explain: Juneau is the capital of Alaska.
questions.q: What is the capital of Alaska?

subject: Kids Geography
title: US States & Capitals
US Regions and Famous Landmarks
subject: Kids Geography
description: Tour the regions of the United States and meet famous landmarks like the Statue of Liberty, the Grand Canyon, and Mount Rushmore.

questions.q: In which city can you visit the Statue of Liberty?
questions.explain: The Statue of Liberty stands on an island in New York Harbor. It was a gift from France and welcomes visitors to New York City.

questions.q: The Grand Canyon is a giant canyon carved by which river?
questions.explain: The Colorado River slowly carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years. The canyon is in the state of Arizona.

questions.q: Mount Rushmore has the faces of four presidents carved into a mountain in which state?
questions.explain: Mount Rushmore shows George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Abraham Lincoln. It is in the Black Hills of South Dakota.

questions.q: Which region of the United States is known for hot deserts like the Mojave?
questions.explain: The Southwest, including Arizona and New Mexico, has dry deserts with cacti. The Northeast is much greener and colder in winter.

questions.q: The Golden Gate Bridge is a famous red-orange bridge in which California city?
questions.explain: The Golden Gate Bridge crosses the bay entrance at San Francisco. Its color is called international orange.

questions.q: Which US region is famous for farming corn and wheat on wide, flat plains?
questions.explain: The Midwest is often called Americas breadbasket because its flat land and rich soil grow huge amounts of food.

questions.q: The Space Needle is a tall tower landmark in which rainy Pacific Northwest city?
questions.explain: The Space Needle was built for a worlds fair in Seattle in 1962. From the top you can see the city, the bay, and mountains.

questions.q: Which landmark is a huge white home in Washington, DC, where the President lives?
questions.explain: The White House is the home and office of the President of the United States. It has been the presidents home since the year 1800.

questions.q: The Gateway Arch, the tallest arch in the world, stands in which Missouri city?
questions.explain: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis is 630 feet tall and honors westward exploration. Visitors can ride a tram to the top.

questions.q: Yellowstone, the first national park in the world, is famous for what spouting hot water feature?
questions.explain: Yellowstone sits over a giant underground volcano and has geysers, including Old Faithful, that shoot hot water into the air.

rounds.title: US Regions and Famous Landmarks
rounds.desc: Tour the regions of the United States and meet famous landmarks like the Statue of Liberty, the Grand Canyon, and Mount Rushmore.

title: Mountains, Rivers and Deserts
subject: Kids Geography
description: Climb the tallest peaks, follow the longest rivers, and cross the driest deserts on a tour of Earths wildest landforms.

questions.q: What is the tallest mountain on Earth?
questions.explain: Mount Everest rises about 29,000 feet in the Himalaya mountains of Asia. Climbers need extra oxygen near its snowy top.

questions.q: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.explain: The Nile flows about 4,100 miles through Africa into the Mediterranean Sea. The Amazon carries more water, but the Nile is a bit longer.

questions.q: The Rocky Mountains run through which side of North America?
questions.explain: The Rockies stretch from Canada down through the western United States. The Appalachian Mountains are the older range in the east.

questions.q: What is a desert?
options: A very dry place that gets little rain
A place that is always hot and sandy
questions.explain: A desert is dry, but it is not always hot or sandy. Antarctica is even called a desert because it gets so little snowfall.

questions.q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explain: The Sahara covers much of northern Africa and is almost as big as the whole United States. It has giant sand dunes and very little rain.

questions.q: The Mississippi River flows into which body of water?
questions.explain: The Mississippi starts in Minnesota and flows south to the Gulf of Mexico. Boats have carried goods along it for hundreds of years.

questions.q: A piece of land with water on all sides is called what?
questions.explain: An island is completely surrounded by water, like Hawaii. A peninsula has water on three sides but connects to land on the fourth.

questions.q: Low land between hills or mountains, often with a river in it, is called a:
questions.explain: Valleys sit between higher land and often have rivers running through them. Many towns and farms are built in valleys.

questions.q: Which mountain is the tallest in North America?
questions.explain: Denali rises over 20,000 feet and is the highest peak in North America. Its name means the high one in a Native Alaskan language.

questions.q: Waterfalls happen when a river:
options: Falls steeply over a cliff or rocks
questions.explain: A waterfall forms where river water drops suddenly over a steep edge. Niagara Falls on the US-Canada border is one of the most famous.

rounds.title: Mountains, Rivers and Deserts
rounds.desc: Climb the tallest peaks, follow the longest rivers, and cross the driest deserts on a tour of Earths wildest landforms.

title: Countries Around the World
subject: Kids Geography
description: Meet countries on every continent: their capitals, languages, and the things that make each place special.

questions.q: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explain: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, the country just north of the United States. Toronto is Canadas biggest city, but it is not the capital.

questions.q: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.explain: On a map, Italy looks like a boot kicking a ball, which is the island of Sicily. Its capital city is Rome.

questions.q: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.explain: Tokyo is the capital of Japan, an island country in Asia. It is one of the largest cities in the world.

questions.q: Which country has the kangaroo and the koala as famous wild animals and the city of Sydney?
questions.explain: Australia is both a continent and a country, famous for kangaroos, koalas, and the Sydney Opera House. Its capital is Canberra.

questions.q: What language do most people speak in Brazil?
questions.explain: Brazil is the largest country in South America and its people speak Portuguese. Most other South American countries speak Spanish.

questions.q: The capital of Egypt, a country with ancient pyramids, is:
questions.explain: Cairo is the capital of Egypt and sits near the famous pyramids of Giza. The Nile River flows through the city.

questions.q: Which country is home to the Great Wall, one of the longest walls ever built?
questions.explain: The Great Wall of China stretches for thousands of miles across northern China. It was built long ago to protect against invaders.

questions.q: What is the capital of France?
questions.explain: Paris is the capital of France and is famous for the Eiffel Tower. People there speak French.

questions.q: Which is the largest country in the world by land area?
questions.explain: Russia is so big it stretches across two continents, Europe and Asia. It has eleven time zones.

questions.q: Mexico City is the capital of which country that borders the United States to the south?
questions.explain: Mexico borders the United States to the south and its capital is Mexico City. People there mostly speak Spanish.

rounds.title: Countries Around the World
rounds.desc: Meet countries on every continent: their capitals, languages, and the things that make each place special.

title: Famous Landmarks and World Wonders
subject: Kids Geography
description: Visit the most famous places humans and nature have made, from the Eiffel Tower and the pyramids to the Great Barrier Reef.

questions.q: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris. In which country is Paris?
questions.explain: The Eiffel Tower was built in Paris, France, in 1889. It was once the tallest human-made structure in the world.

questions.q: The ancient pyramids of Giza were built in which country?
questions.explain: The pyramids of Giza in Egypt were built about 4,500 years ago as tombs for kings. The Great Pyramid was the tallest building on Earth for thousands of years.

questions.q: The Taj Mahal, a beautiful white marble building, is in which Asian country?
questions.explain: The Taj Mahal in India was built by an emperor to honor his wife. Its white marble changes color with the light of the day.

questions.q: Which famous statue in Brazil stands with open arms on a mountain above Rio de Janeiro?
questions.explain: Christ the Redeemer is a huge statue of Jesus on Corcovado Mountain in Brazil. It is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

questions.q: The Colosseum, where ancient Romans watched games, is in which city?
questions.explain: The Colosseum in Rome could hold about 50,000 people. It opened almost 2,000 years ago in the year 80.

questions.q: The Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef on Earth, is near the coast of which country?
questions.explain: The Great Barrier Reef off Australia is so big it can be seen from space. Thousands of sea animals live in its colorful coral.

questions.q: Machu Picchu is an ancient stone city high in the mountains of which South American country?
questions.explain: The Inca people built Machu Picchu in the Andes Mountains of Peru about 600 years ago. No one knows exactly why it was built.

questions.q: The Great Sphinx in Egypt has the body of which animal?
questions.explain: The Sphinx has the body of a lion and the head of a human. It guards the pyramids at Giza and is carved from one huge rock.

questions.q: Which natural wonder is a super-deep canyon lake in Russia, the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explain: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest and oldest lake on Earth. In winter its ice is so clear you can see far down through it.

questions.q: Big Ben is the nickname of a famous clock tower in which city?
questions.explain: Big Ben is actually the name of the great bell inside the tower in London. The tower stands next to the River Thames.

rounds.title: Famous Landmarks and World Wonders
rounds.desc: Visit the most famous places humans and nature have made, from the Eiffel Tower and the pyramids to the Great Barrier Reef.

title: Flags of the World
subject: Kids Geography
description: Have fun with flags: spot the animals, stars, stripes, and colors countries use to tell their stories.

questions.q: The flag of the United States has how many stars?
questions.explain: The American flag has 50 stars, one for each state. The 13 stripes stand for the first 13 colonies.

questions.q: Which countrys flag is a red circle on a white background, like the sun?
questions.explain: Japans flag shows a red sun disc on white. Japan is sometimes called the Land of the Rising Sun.

questions.q: Canadas flag has which leaf in the middle?
questions.explain: A red maple leaf sits in the center of Canadas flag. Maple trees grow all over Canada and maple syrup is a famous Canadian treat.

questions.q: Which countrys flag has a red dragon on it?
questions.explain: The flag of Wales shows a red dragon, a symbol from old Welsh stories. Wales is part of the United Kingdom.

questions.q: The flag of Mexico has which bird in the center, holding a snake?
questions.explain: Mexicos flag shows an eagle on a cactus holding a snake, from an Aztec legend about where to build their city.

questions.q: How many stars are on the flag of China?
questions.explain: Chinas red flag has five gold stars in one corner: one big star and four small ones.

questions.q: Which countrys flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle or square, shaped instead like two triangles?
questions.explain: Nepals flag is made of two stacked triangles, making it unique in the world. It shows a sun and a moon.

questions.q: The flag of Brazil has a blue circle that looks like:
options: A globe of stars with a banner across it
questions.explain: Brazils flag has a green field, a yellow diamond, and a blue globe showing stars of the southern sky. A banner on it says Order and Progress.

questions.q: What three colors are on the flag of France?
questions.explain: Frances flag has three vertical stripes: blue, white, and red. Italy uses green, white, and red instead.

questions.q: Switzerlands flag is special because it is:
options: A square with a white cross on red
The longest flag in the world
questions.explain: Switzerland and Vatican City have the only square national flags. The white cross on red is also the symbol of the Red Cross in reverse colors.

rounds.title: Flags of the World
rounds.desc: Have fun with flags: spot the animals, stars, stripes, and colors countries use to tell their stories.

title: World Explorers Challenge
subject: Kids Geography
description: A final mixed challenge: biggest, longest, deepest, and most surprising geography facts from all over the world.

questions.q: Which desert is the driest place on Earth, where some spots have almost never had rain?
questions.explain: Parts of the Atacama Desert in South America have gone years without rain. Scientists test Mars rovers there because it is so Mars-like.

questions.q: What is the deepest place in the oceans?
options: The middle of the Atlantic Ocean
The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean
questions.explain: The Mariana Trench is so deep that Mount Everest would fit inside it with room to spare. Only a few explorers have ever reached its bottom.

questions.q: Which country has more people than any other in the world today?
questions.explain: India passed China in 2023 to become the country with the most people, over 1.4 billion. That is more than four times the people in the United States.

questions.q: The Amazon Rainforest, the biggest rainforest on Earth, is mostly in which country?
questions.explain: About 60 percent of the Amazon Rainforest lies in Brazil. The forest makes much of the Earths oxygen and is home to one in ten known species.

questions.q: Which is the smallest continent?
questions.explain: Australia is the smallest continent, though it is still a huge island country. Europe is the second smallest.

questions.q: Iceland is a country famous for:
options: Volcanoes and hot springs called geysers
questions.explain: Iceland sits on top of underground volcanic heat, giving it erupting volcanoes and steaming hot springs. Its capital is Reykjavik.

questions.q: Madagascar, one of the biggest islands in the world, sits in the ocean off the coast of which continent?
questions.explain: Madagascar lies in the Indian Ocean just off the southeast coast of Africa. Many of its animals, like lemurs, live nowhere else on Earth.

questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro, a snow-capped mountain near the equator, is in which African country?
questions.explain: Kilimanjaro is the tallest mountain in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world. Its snowy top is surprising because it sits near the hot equator.

questions.q: Which ocean is the smallest and shallowest?
questions.explain: The Arctic Ocean around the North Pole is the smallest ocean and is covered by sea ice for much of the year.

questions.q: The Danube is a famous long river that flows through many countries on which continent?
questions.explain: The Danube flows through ten European countries, more than any other river in the world, including Germany, Austria, and Hungary.

rounds.title: World Explorers Challenge
rounds.desc: A final mixed challenge: biggest, longest, deepest, and most surprising geography facts from all over the world.

title: Number Sense and Place Value
subject: Pre-Algebra
description: Place value, comparing numbers, rounding, and how whole numbers are built.

questions.q: In the number 4,582, what is the value of the digit 5?
questions.explain: The 5 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 5 x 100 = 500.

questions.q: Which number is greatest?
questions.explain: Compare from the left: 3,904 has 9 in the hundreds place, the largest hundreds digit.

questions.q: Round 6,738 to the nearest hundred.
questions.explain: The tens digit is 3, so 6,738 rounds down to 6,700.

questions.q: How is 30,000 + 4,000 + 200 + 9 written as a standard number?
Which symbol makes 0.7 ___ 0.07 true?
questions.explain: 0.7 is seven tenths, which is greater than seven hundredths (0.07).

questions.q: What is the place value of 8 in 12.83?
questions.explain: The first digit after the decimal point is in the tenths place.

questions.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
questions.explain: Compare tenths first: 2.05 is smallest, then 2.5, then 2.55.

questions.q: Round 49.6 to the nearest whole number.
questions.explain: The tenths digit is 6, so 49.6 rounds up to 50.

questions.q: A number has 6 tens, 3 ones, and 4 hundreds. What is the number?
questions.explain: 4 hundreds + 6 tens + 3 ones = 400 + 60 + 3 = 463.

questions.q: Which number is between 1,200 and 1,300?
questions.explain: 1,250 is greater than 1,200 and less than 1,300.

rounds.title: Number Sense and Place Value
rounds.desc: Place value, comparing numbers, rounding, and how whole numbers are built.

title: Fractions Basics
subject: Pre-Algebra
description: What fractions mean, equivalent fractions, comparing fractions, and simple fraction operations.

questions.q: In the fraction 3/8, the number 3 is called the:
questions.explain: The numerator is the top number; it tells how many parts are counted.

questions.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3?
questions.explain: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2: 2/3 = 4/6.

questions.q: Simplify 6/9 to lowest terms.
questions.explain: Divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 3.

questions.q: Which fraction is larger?
questions.explain: With the same numerator, the smaller denominator means larger pieces.

questions.q: What is 1/5 + 2/5?
questions.explain: With like denominators, add the numerators and keep the denominator.

questions.q: Write 7/4 as a mixed number.
questions.explain: 7 divided by 4 is 1 with remainder 3, so 7/4 = 1 3/4.

questions.q: Which fraction equals one whole?
questions.explain: When numerator equals denominator, the fraction equals 1.

questions.q: What is 3/4 - 1/4?
questions.explain: 3/4 - 1/4 = 2/4, which simplifies to 1/2.

questions.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. You eat 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did you eat?
questions.explain: You ate 3 out of 8 equal parts, written as 3/8.

questions.q: Which is an improper fraction?
questions.explain: An improper fraction has a numerator greater than its denominator.

rounds.title: Fractions Basics
rounds.desc: What fractions mean, equivalent fractions, comparing fractions, and simple fraction operations.

title: Decimals and Percents
subject: Pre-Algebra
description: Converting between decimals, fractions, and percents, and finding a percent of a number.

questions.q: Write 0.25 as a percent.
questions.explain: Move the decimal point two places right: 0.25 = 25%.

questions.q: Write 3/5 as a decimal.
questions.explain: Divide 3 by 5 to get 0.6.

questions.q: What is 50% of 80?
questions.explain: 50% is one half, and half of 80 is 40.

questions.q: Write 75% as a fraction in simplest form.
questions.explain: 75% = 75/100, which simplifies to 3/4.

questions.q: Which decimal equals 1/10?
questions.explain: One tenth is written as 0.1.

questions.q: A shirt costs $20 and is on sale for 10% off. How much is the discount?
Write 0.07 as a percent.
What is 1/4 written as a percent?
Which is greatest?
questions.explain: 0.5 = 50%, which is greater than 45%, 25%, and 5%.

questions.q: What is 20% of 50?

rounds.title: Decimals and Percents
rounds.desc: Converting between decimals, fractions, and percents, and finding a percent of a number.

description: Negative numbers, absolute value, and adding and subtracting integers.

questions.explain: Adding -3 moves you 3 steps left from 5 on the number line, so 5 + (-3) = 2.
questions.q: What is 5 + (-3)?

questions.explain: Both numbers are negative, so add their sizes and keep the minus sign: 4 + 6 = 10, so the answer is -10.
questions.q: What is -4 + (-6)?

questions.explain: Absolute value is the distance from 0, and distance is never negative, so |-9| = 9.
questions.q: What is the absolute value of -9?

questions.explain: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding a positive: 3 - (-5) = 3 + 5 = 8.
questions.q: What is 3 - (-5)?

questions.explain: -7 sits farthest to the left on the number line, so it is the smallest of the four.
questions.q: Which number is the smallest?

questions.explain: Start at -8 and move 3 steps to the right: -8 + 3 = -5.
questions.q: What is -8 + 3?

questions.explain: Start at -6 and move 4 more steps to the left: -6 - 4 = -10.
questions.q: What is -6 - 4?

questions.explain: The opposite of a number has the same size but the other sign, so the opposite of 12 is -12.
questions.q: What is the opposite of 12?

questions.explain: A negative times a negative gives a positive, and 3 x 4 = 12, so -3 x -4 = 12.
questions.q: What is -3 x -4?

questions.explain: Start at -2 and add the rise of 9: -2 + 9 = 7 degrees.
questions.q: The temperature was -2 degrees in the morning and rose 9 degrees by noon. What was the temperature at noon?

subject: Pre-Algebra
title: Integers

description: Simplifying ratios, unit rates, and solving simple proportions.

questions.explain: Divide both numbers by 3: 6 / 3 = 2 and 9 / 3 = 3, so 6:9 simplifies to 2:3.
questions.q: Write the ratio 6:9 in simplest form.

questions.explain: Divide the total cost by the number of markers: 2 / 4 = 0.50, so each marker costs $0.50.
questions.q: 4 markers cost $2 in total. What is the cost per marker?

questions.explain: Multiply the top and bottom of 4/5 by 2: (4 x 2) / (5 x 2) = 8/10.
questions.q: Which ratio is equal to 4/5?

questions.explain: Cross-multiply to get 2x = 18, so x = 9. Check: 9/6 simplifies to 3/2.
questions.q: Solve for x: x/6 = 3/2.

questions.explain: Divide the miles by the hours: 150 / 3 = 50 mph.
questions.q: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. What is its speed in miles per hour?

questions.explain: 15 dogs is 3 groups of 5, so scale the cats by 3 as well: 3 x 3 = 9 cats.
questions.q: The ratio of cats to dogs at a shelter is 3:5. If there are 15 dogs, how many cats are there?

questions.explain: Divide both numbers by 4: 12 / 4 = 3 and 4 / 4 = 1, so 12:4 simplifies to 3:1.
questions.q: Simplify the ratio 12:4.

questions.explain: The first deal is 3 / 6 = $0.50 per apple. The second is 6 / 10 = $0.60 per apple, so the 6-pack is the better buy.
questions.q: Which is the better buy: 6 apples for $3 or 10 apples for $6?

questions.explain: Divide the top and bottom by 5: 15 / 5 = 3 and 25 / 5 = 5, so 15/25 = 3/5.
questions.q: Write 15/25 in simplest form.

questions.explain: Multiply the inches by the miles per inch: 4 x 20 = 80 miles.
questions.q: On a map, 1 inch stands for 20 miles. How many miles do 4 inches stand for?

subject: Pre-Algebra
title: Ratios & Proportions

description: Exponents, perfect squares, and square roots.

questions.explain: 3^2 means 3 x 3, which equals 9. The exponent tells you how many times to multiply the base by itself.
questions.q: What is 3^2?

questions.explain: 2^3 means 2 x 2 x 2. First 2 x 2 = 4, then 4 x 2 = 8.
questions.q: What is 2^3?

questions.explain: A square root asks what number times itself gives the value: 7 x 7 = 49, so sqrt(49) = 7.
questions.q: What is sqrt(49)?

questions.explain: 10^2 means 10 x 10, which equals 100.
questions.q: What is 10^2?

questions.explain: Do the power first: 5^2 = 25. Then add 1: 25 + 1 = 26.
questions.q: What is 5^2 + 1?
What is sqrt(81)?

questions.explain: 2^4 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 16. The others give 8, 9, and 64.
questions.q: Which power equals 16?

questions.explain: Any number raised to the power of 1 is itself, so 7^1 = 7.
questions.q: What is 7^1?

questions.explain: 4^2 means 4 x 4, which equals 16. Do not just double the base.
questions.q: What is 4^2?
What is sqrt(144)?

subject: Pre-Algebra
title: Powers & Roots
Expressions and Order of Operations
subject: Pre-Algebra
description: Evaluating expressions, using PEMDAS, and translating words into algebra.

questions.q: Evaluate: 3 + 4 x 2.
questions.explain: Multiply first: 4 x 2 = 8, then 3 + 8 = 11.

questions.q: Evaluate: (3 + 4) x 2.
questions.explain: Parentheses first: 3 + 4 = 7, then 7 x 2 = 14.

questions.q: If x = 5, what is 2x + 3?
Which expression means '5 more than a number n'?
questions.explain: 'More than' means addition: n + 5.

questions.q: Evaluate: 20 - 4 / 2.
questions.explain: Divide first: 4 / 2 = 2, then 20 - 2 = 18.

questions.q: Simplify: 3a + 2a.
questions.explain: Combine like terms: 3a + 2a = 5a.

questions.q: Evaluate: 2 x (6 - 3) + 1.
questions.explain: Parentheses: 6 - 3 = 3; 2 x 3 = 6; 6 + 1 = 7.

questions.q: Which expression means 'the product of 7 and y'?
questions.explain: Product means multiplication, written as 7y.

questions.q: If a = 2 and b = 3, what is a + b x 2?
questions.explain: Multiply first: 3 x 2 = 6, then 2 + 6 = 8.

questions.q: Evaluate: 15 / 3 + 2 x 4.

rounds.title: Expressions and Order of Operations
rounds.desc: Evaluating expressions, using PEMDAS, and translating words into algebra.

title: Solving One-Step Equations
subject: Pre-Algebra
description: Undoing addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division to isolate a variable.

questions.q: Solve: x + 7 = 12.
questions.explain: Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 12 - 7 = 5.

questions.q: Solve: x - 4 = 9.
questions.explain: Add 4 to both sides: x = 9 + 4 = 13.

questions.q: Solve: 3x = 18.
questions.explain: Divide both sides by 3: x = 18 / 3 = 6.

questions.q: Solve: x / 5 = 4.
questions.explain: Multiply both sides by 5: x = 4 x 5 = 20.

questions.q: Solve: x + 15 = 15.
questions.explain: Subtract 15 from both sides: x = 0.

questions.q: Which operation undoes multiplication by 4?
questions.explain: Inverse operations undo each other: division undoes multiplication.

questions.q: Solve: 2x + 1 = 9 (two steps).
questions.explain: Subtract 1 to get 2x = 8, then divide by 2 to get x = 4.

questions.q: Solve: x - 10 = -3.
questions.explain: Add 10 to both sides: x = -3 + 10 = 7.

questions.q: A number increased by 8 equals 20. Which equation matches?
questions.explain: 'Increased by 8' means add 8 to the number.

questions.q: Solve: 5x = 0.
questions.explain: Divide both sides by 5: x = 0 / 5 = 0.

rounds.title: Solving One-Step Equations
rounds.desc: Undoing addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division to isolate a variable.

title: Graphing on the Coordinate Plane
subject: Pre-Algebra
description: Reading points, quadrants, and simple patterns on an x-y grid.

questions.q: In the ordered pair (3, 5), which number is the x-coordinate?
questions.explain: Ordered pairs are written (x, y), so the first number is x.

questions.q: The point (0, 0) is called the:
questions.explain: The origin is where the x-axis and y-axis cross.

questions.q: In which quadrant is the point (-2, 3)?
questions.explain: Quadrant II has negative x values and positive y values.

questions.q: What are the coordinates of a point 4 units right and 2 units up from the origin?
questions.explain: Move right 4 for x, then up 2 for y: (4, 2).

questions.q: The horizontal number line on a graph is the:
questions.explain: The x-axis runs horizontally; the y-axis runs vertically.

questions.q: Which point lies on the y-axis?
questions.explain: Points on the y-axis have an x-coordinate of 0.

questions.q: If a point has coordinates (-3, -1), it is in:
questions.explain: Quadrant III has both coordinates negative.

questions.q: Starting at (1, 1), move right 3 and up 2. Where do you end?
questions.explain: Add 3 to x (1+3=4) and 2 to y (1+2=3).

questions.q: A graph shows y = x + 1. When x = 4, what is y?
questions.explain: Substitute: y = 4 + 1 = 5.

questions.q: The vertical number line on a graph is the:
questions.explain: The y-axis runs vertically through the origin.

rounds.title: Graphing on the Coordinate Plane
rounds.desc: Reading points, quadrants, and simple patterns on an x-y grid.

title: Geometry Basics
subject: Pre-Algebra
description: Angles, triangles, perimeter, area, and basic shapes.

questions.q: How many degrees are in a right angle?
questions.explain: A right angle, like the corner of a square, measures 90 degrees.

questions.q: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 6 units long and 3 units wide?
questions.explain: Perimeter = 2(6 + 3) = 18 units.

questions.q: What is the area of a square with side length 5?
questions.explain: Area of a square = side x side = 5 x 5 = 25.

questions.q: A triangle with all three sides equal is called:
questions.explain: Equilateral triangles have three equal sides and three equal angles.

questions.q: How many degrees do the angles inside a triangle add up to?
questions.explain: The interior angles of any triangle sum to 180 degrees.

questions.q: An angle smaller than 90 degrees is called:
questions.explain: Acute angles measure more than 0 and less than 90 degrees.

questions.q: What is the area of a triangle with base 8 and height 4?
questions.explain: Area = (base x height) / 2 = (8 x 4) / 2 = 16.

questions.q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
questions.explain: A pentagon has five sides; a hexagon has six.

questions.q: A straight angle measures:
questions.explain: A straight angle forms a straight line and measures 180 degrees.

questions.q: The distance around a circle is called its:
questions.explain: Circumference is the perimeter of a circle.

rounds.title: Geometry Basics
rounds.desc: Angles, triangles, perimeter, area, and basic shapes.

title: Points, Lines and Planes
subject: Geometry
description: Build the foundation of geometry: points, lines, segments, rays, and planes, plus how to measure segments and find midpoints.

questions.q: What is a point in geometry?
options: A flat surface that extends forever
A location with no size, shown as a dot
questions.explain: A point marks an exact location and has no length, width, or thickness. Points are named with capital letters.

questions.q: What is a line segment?
options: Part of a line with two endpoints
A line that extends forever both ways
A part of a line with one endpoint
questions.explain: A segment has a definite length because it stops at two endpoints. A full line, by contrast, goes on forever in both directions.

questions.q: What is a ray?
options: Part of a line with one endpoint that extends forever in one direction
A flat surface with no thickness
questions.explain: A ray starts at its endpoint and continues endlessly in one direction. Sunlight is often compared to rays starting at the sun.

questions.q: Point M is the midpoint of segment AB. If AM is 7 cm, what is the length of AB?
questions.explain: A midpoint splits a segment into two equal parts, so AB is 7 plus 7, which is 14 cm. Doubling one half gives the whole segment.

questions.q: What is a plane in geometry?
options: A flat surface that extends forever in all directions
questions.explain: A plane is like an endless flat sheet with length and width but no thickness. A tabletop models part of a plane.

questions.q: Two points are 3 cm and 11 cm from the left end of a segment on a number line at positions 3 and 11. What is the distance between them?
questions.explain: Distance is the absolute difference of the positions: 11 minus 3 equals 8 cm. Distance is always positive.

questions.q: Which statement is true about two intersecting lines?
options: They cross at exactly one point
questions.explain: Two different straight lines in a plane can meet at most once. Lines that never meet are parallel.

questions.q: A segment has endpoints at positions 2 and 10 on a number line. Where is its midpoint?
questions.explain: Average the endpoints: 2 plus 10 equals 12, and 12 divided by 2 equals 6. The midpoint is the same distance from both ends.

questions.q: What does it mean when two segments are congruent?
options: They lie on the same line
They have exactly the same length
questions.explain: Congruent segments can be placed in different positions but measure the same. Tick marks on a diagram show equal lengths.

questions.q: Segment PQ is 18 cm long. Point R lies on it so that PR is twice as long as RQ. How long is RQ?
questions.explain: Let RQ be x, so PR is 2x, and x plus 2x equals 18, giving 3x equals 18 and x equals 6 cm. Check: 12 plus 6 equals 18.

questions.q: Two angles form a linear pair. If one measures 115 degrees, what does the other measure?
questions.explain: Angles in a linear pair are supplementary and add to 180 degrees: 180 minus 115 equals 65 degrees.

questions.q: What are vertical angles?
options: Opposite angles formed by two crossing lines, and they are equal
Angles side by side on a straight line
questions.explain: When two lines cross, the angles across from each other are vertical angles. Vertical angles always have equal measures.

questions.q: Two lines are cut by a transversal. A corresponding angle measures 70 degrees. What is the measure of the matching corresponding angle if the lines are parallel?
questions.explain: Corresponding angles formed by parallel lines are equal. Both sit in the same corner position at each crossing.

questions.q: Alternate interior angles are located:
options: Outside the lines on the same side
Inside the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal
questions.explain: Alternate interior angles lie between the two lines and switch sides of the transversal. With parallel lines, they are equal.

questions.q: Same-side interior angles cut by a transversal across parallel lines add up to:
questions.explain: Same-side interior angles are supplementary when lines are parallel. For example, 110 degrees pairs with 70 degrees.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 3x degrees and its corresponding angle is 75 degrees. What is x?
questions.explain: Corresponding angles are equal, so 3x equals 75, and dividing by 3 gives x equals 25. Always set equal angles equal to each other.

questions.q: An angle and its supplement are equal in measure. What is the measure of each angle?
questions.explain: If x plus x equals 180, then 2x equals 180 and x equals 90 degrees. Two equal supplementary angles must both be right angles.

questions.q: Which pair of angles is complementary?
questions.explain: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees, and 30 plus 60 equals 90. Supplementary angles, by contrast, add to 180 degrees.

questions.q: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 5x degrees and its same-side interior partner measures 110 degrees. What is x?
questions.explain: Same-side interior angles are supplementary, so 5x plus 110 equals 180, giving 5x equals 70 and x equals 14.

questions.q: A transversal crosses parallel lines. One angle is 2x plus 20 degrees and the vertical angle to its corresponding partner is 100 degrees. What is x?
questions.explain: The angle equals its corresponding partner, so 2x plus 20 equals 100, giving 2x equals 80 and x equals 40. Vertical and corresponding relationships both preserve equality here.

description: Tell congruent figures from similar ones, use scale factors, and solve for missing sides in similar triangles.

questions.q: What does it mean for two figures to be congruent?
options: They have the same shape but different sizes
They have the same shape and the same size
They have the same area only
questions.explain: Congruent figures match exactly when placed on top of each other. Every side and angle is equal.

questions.q: Two triangles are similar. What must be true?
options: Their corresponding angles are equal and their sides are in proportion
questions.explain: Similarity keeps the shape but can change the size. Angles stay equal while sides scale by the same ratio.

questions.q: A triangle has sides 3, 4, and 5. A similar triangle has a shortest side of 6. What is the scale factor from small to large?
questions.explain: Divide the new shortest side by the original: 6 divided by 3 equals a scale factor of 2. Every side of the larger triangle is twice as long.

questions.q: A triangle with longest side 5 is enlarged by a scale factor of 2. What is the longest side of the larger triangle?
questions.explain: Multiply the longest side by the scale factor: 5 times 2 equals 10. Apply the same scale factor to every side.

questions.q: Two congruent triangles have one side of 8 cm in the first. How long is the matching side in the second?
questions.explain: Congruent figures have equal corresponding parts, so the matching side is also 8 cm. This is often shortened to CPCTC in proofs.

questions.q: A photo 4 inches wide and 6 inches tall is enlarged so the width becomes 10 inches. What is the new height?
questions.explain: The scale factor is 10 divided by 4, which is 2.5, and 6 times 2.5 equals 15 inches. Both dimensions grow by the same factor.

questions.q: Which test can prove two triangles congruent?
options: Two sides equal but angles ignored
Side-Side-Side: all three pairs of sides are equal
questions.explain: SSS proves congruence because equal sides fix the triangles shape and size. AAA only proves similarity, since size can still change.

questions.q: Similar rectangles have widths 5 and 15. The smaller has length 8. What is the length of the larger?
questions.explain: The scale factor is 15 divided by 5, which is 3, so the length is 8 times 3, which is 24. Set up a proportion to solve problems like this reliably.

questions.q: A map uses a scale where 1 cm represents 5 km. Two towns are 7 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life?
questions.explain: Multiply 7 cm by 5 km per cm to get 35 km. Map scales are proportions between drawing distance and real distance.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have perimeters 18 and 54. A side of the small triangle is 5. What is the matching side of the large triangle?
questions.explain: The perimeter ratio is 54 divided by 18, which is 3, so sides scale by 3 as well: 5 times 3 equals 15. Perimeters scale by the same factor as sides.

description: Plot points, find distances and midpoints on the coordinate plane, and use slopes to describe lines.

questions.q: In the point (4, -3), what is the y-coordinate?
questions.explain: Points are written as (x, y), so the second number is the y-coordinate. Here the y-coordinate is -3, which places the point below the x-axis.

questions.q: What is the distance between (1, 2) and (4, 6)?
questions.explain: Use the distance formula: the x difference is 3 and the y difference is 4, and 3 squared plus 4 squared equals 25, whose square root is 5 units.

questions.q: What is the midpoint of the segment joining (2, 4) and (8, 10)?
questions.explain: Average each pair of coordinates: (2 plus 8) divided by 2 equals 5, and (4 plus 10) divided by 2 equals 7, giving (5, 7).

questions.q: What is the slope of the line through (0, 1) and (3, 7)?
questions.explain: Slope is rise over run: (7 minus 1) divided by (3 minus 0) equals 6 divided by 3, which is 2.

questions.q: A line has slope 3 and passes through the origin. What is the y-value when x is 4?
questions.explain: The line is y equals 3x, so when x is 4, y equals 3 times 4, which is 12. The origin means the y-intercept is 0.

questions.q: Which point lies in Quadrant II?
questions.explain: Quadrant II is the top-left region where x is negative and y is positive. The point (-5, 2) fits that pattern.

questions.q: What is the distance between (-2, 3) and (-2, 9)?
questions.explain: The x-coordinates match, so the distance is just the difference in y: 9 minus 3 equals 6 units. Vertical distances only need the y change.

questions.q: Two lines have slopes 2 and 2. What is true about them?
options: They are the same line for sure
They cross at a right angle
questions.explain: Parallel lines have equal slopes. Unless every point matches, equal slopes mean the lines never meet.

questions.q: What is the midpoint of (-4, 6) and (4, -2)?
questions.explain: Average the x values: (-4 plus 4) divided by 2 equals 0, and average the y values: (6 plus -2) divided by 2 equals 2, giving (0, 2).

questions.q: The slope of a line through (2, 5) and (6, 5) is:
questions.explain: The y values do not change, so the rise is 0 and the slope is 0 divided by 4, which is 0. Horizontal lines always have slope 0.

title: Transformations and Symmetry
subject: Geometry
description: Slide, flip, turn, and resize shapes, track coordinates through transformations, and recognize lines of symmetry.

questions.q: What is a translation?
options: A slide that moves every point of a figure the same distance and direction
questions.explain: A translation slides a figure without rotating or flipping it. The figure keeps the same size, shape, and orientation.

questions.q: Point (3, 5) is translated 4 units right and 2 units down. What are the new coordinates?
questions.explain: Moving right adds to x: 3 plus 4 equals 7. Moving down subtracts from y: 5 minus 2 equals 3, giving (7, 3).

questions.q: What is a reflection?
options: A slide in a straight line
A flip of a figure over a line, creating a mirror image
questions.explain: A reflection flips a figure across a mirror line. Each point ends up the same distance from the line on the other side.

questions.q: Point (2, 6) is reflected over the x-axis. What are the new coordinates?
questions.explain: Reflecting over the x-axis keeps x the same and flips the sign of y, so (2, 6) becomes (2, -6).

questions.q: A rotation of 180 degrees about the origin sends (4, -1) to which point?
questions.explain: A half-turn about the origin flips the signs of both coordinates, so (4, -1) becomes (-4, 1).

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explain: A square can be folded along both diagonals and both midlines, giving 4 lines of symmetry. Each fold maps one half exactly onto the other.

questions.q: What is a dilation?
options: A transformation that resizes a figure by a scale factor from a center point
questions.explain: Dilations grow or shrink a figure while keeping its shape. A scale factor above 1 enlarges and below 1 shrinks.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has a vertex at (1, 2). After a dilation centered at the origin with scale factor 3, where is that vertex?
questions.explain: Multiply both coordinates by the scale factor: 1 times 3 is 3 and 2 times 3 is 6, giving (3, 6).

questions.q: Which transformation does NOT preserve a figures size?
options: Dilation with a scale factor other than 1
questions.explain: Translations, reflections, and rotations are rigid motions that keep size and shape. A dilation changes size unless the scale factor is exactly 1.

questions.q: A figure is translated from (0, 0) to (5, -3), then reflected over the y-axis. Where does the original point (0, 0) end up?
questions.explain: First the point moves to (5, -3). Reflecting over the y-axis flips the x sign, giving (-5, -3).

title: Geometric Proofs and Reasoning
subject: Geometry
description: Learn how statements, reasons, and theorems fit together, and practice multi-step deductions about angles and triangles.

questions.q: What is a conjecture in geometry?
options: A statement believed to be true based on observations, but not yet proven
A fact that needs no checking ever
questions.explain: A conjecture is an educated guess from patterns you notice. It becomes a theorem only after a valid proof.

questions.q: What does a proof do?
options: Shows one example where a statement works
Uses logic and known facts to show a statement must be true
Asks classmates to vote on a statement
Measures a single drawing with a ruler
questions.explain: A proof is a chain of logical steps from givens and known theorems. One example can support an idea but never proves it for all cases.

questions.q: If all squares are rectangles, and figure F is a square, what can you conclude?
options: Figure F has no right angles
questions.explain: This is deductive reasoning: apply the general rule to the specific case. The conclusion that F is a rectangle must be true.

questions.q: What is a counterexample?
options: An example that shows a statement is false
questions.explain: One counterexample is enough to disprove a claim. For instance, a rectangle that is not a square disproves the claim that all rectangles are squares.

questions.q: Angles A and B are supplementary and angle A is 4 times angle B. What is the measure of angle B?
questions.explain: Write B plus 4B equals 180, so 5B equals 180 and B equals 36 degrees. Then angle A is 144 degrees, and 36 plus 144 equals 180.

questions.q: In a two-column proof, where do the reasons go?
options: In the right column, matched to each statement on the left
questions.explain: Each statement on the left needs a reason on the right, such as a given, a definition, or a theorem. The matching rows make the logic easy to check.

questions.q: The exterior angle of a triangle equals 130 degrees and one remote interior angle is 55 degrees. What is the other remote interior angle?
questions.explain: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 130 minus 55 equals 75 degrees.

questions.q: If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, what can you conclude about the third angles?
questions.explain: Since each triangles angles sum to 180 degrees, equal pairs force the third angles to match as well. This fact supports the Angle-Angle similarity rule.

questions.q: A triangle has angles in the ratio 2 to 3 to 4. What is the largest angle?
questions.explain: The parts sum to 2 plus 3 plus 4, which is 9, and 180 divided by 9 is 20, so the largest angle is 4 times 20, which is 80 degrees.

questions.q: To prove two segments are equal in length using coordinates (-1, 2), (3, 2) and (0, 5), (4, 5): what is the shared length?
questions.explain: Each segment is horizontal, so length is the x difference: 3 minus -1 equals 4, and 4 minus 0 equals 4. Equal lengths complete the proof step.

title: Trigonometry Introduction
subject: Geometry
description: Meet sine, cosine, and tangent, then use them with the Pythagorean theorem to solve multi-step right triangle problems.

questions.q: In a right triangle, the sine of an angle is defined as:
options: Opposite side divided by adjacent side
questions.explain: Sine compares the side across from the angle to the longest side. Remember the trio with SOH-CAH-TOA.

questions.q: In a right triangle, the tangent of an angle is defined as:
options: Opposite side divided by adjacent side
questions.explain: Tangent is opposite over adjacent, the TOA part of SOH-CAH-TOA. It does not use the hypotenuse.

questions.q: A right triangle has an angle of 30 degrees and a hypotenuse of 10. Using sin 30 degrees equals 0.5, what is the length of the side opposite the 30 degree angle?
questions.explain: Sine equals opposite over hypotenuse, so opposite equals 0.5 times 10, which is 5. Rearranging the ratio is the key step.

questions.q: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. What is the hypotenuse, and what is sin of the angle opposite the side of length 5?
questions.explain: First 5 squared plus 12 squared equals 169, whose square root is 13. Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, so it is 5 divided by 13.

questions.q: A 12 foot ladder leans against a wall and makes a 60 degree angle with the ground. Using cos 60 degrees equals 0.5, how far is the foot of the ladder from the wall?
questions.explain: The distance from the wall is the adjacent side: adjacent equals cos 60 times hypotenuse, which is 0.5 times 12, equaling 6 feet.

questions.q: An angle of elevation is measured:
options: Upward from a horizontal line to an object above
questions.explain: Angles of elevation look up from the horizontal, while angles of depression look down. Both appear in real survey and navigation problems.

questions.q: A right triangle has an adjacent side of 8 and hypotenuse of 10 for angle A. What is cos A?
questions.explain: Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse: 8 divided by 10 equals 0.8. Ratios in trig are unit-free numbers.

questions.q: A kite string makes a 45 degree angle with the ground. Using tan 45 degrees equals 1, if the kite is directly above a point 40 meters from you horizontally, how high is the kite?
questions.explain: Tangent equals opposite over adjacent, so height equals tan 45 times 40, which is 1 times 40, equaling 40 meters.

questions.q: A right triangle has an angle with opposite side 9 and adjacent side 12. What is tan of that angle, and what is the hypotenuse?
questions.explain: Tangent is 9 divided by 12, which is 0.75. The hypotenuse comes from 9 squared plus 12 squared equals 225, whose square root is 15.

questions.q: A ramp must rise 3 feet over a horizontal run where the angle satisfies tan equals 3 divided by 12. A builder says the angle ratio shows a gentle ramp. What is the tangent value and the run if the rise doubles to 6 feet at the same angle?
questions.explain: Tangent is 3 divided by 12, which is 0.25. At the same angle, run equals rise divided by tangent: 6 divided by 0.25 equals 24 feet.

questions.q: What is the main job of a bank?
options: To keep money safe and help people save, borrow, and pay
To print new money for anyone who asks
To decide how much tax you pay
questions.explain: Banks safeguard deposits and provide accounts, cards, and loans. The government, not banks, prints money.

questions.q: What is a checking account mainly used for?
options: Storing money you never touch for 30 years
questions.explain: Checking accounts are built for frequent deposits and payments. Savings accounts are better for money you want to keep and grow.

questions.q: What does a debit card do when you buy something?
options: It borrows money you pay back later
It adds points that become cash automatically
It takes money directly out of your checking account
It uses money from a savings bond
questions.explain: A debit card spends your own money right away. A credit card, by contrast, borrows money from the card company.

questions.q: What does ATM stand for?
questions.explain: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine. It lets you withdraw cash and check balances without going inside a bank.

questions.q: Your bank balance is 240 dollars and you deposit a 60 dollar paycheck. What is your new balance?
questions.explain: Add the deposit to the balance: 240 plus 60 equals 300 dollars. Deposits increase your balance and withdrawals decrease it.

questions.q: What is an overdraft fee?
options: A reward for saving a lot
A charge when you spend more money than your account has
A fee for opening a savings account
A tax on ATM withdrawals only
questions.explain: If you spend more than your balance, the bank may cover the purchase and charge an overdraft fee. Watching your balance helps you avoid it.

questions.q: Why should you use a PIN that is hard to guess?
options: It makes your card work faster
It helps protect your account from people who find or steal your card
questions.explain: A private PIN adds a layer of protection for your card and account. Never share your PIN or use easy guesses like your birth year.

questions.q: Maya checks her account and sees a 35 dollar charge she never made. What should she do first?
options: Ignore it and hope it disappears
Pay it so the bank is not upset
Close every account she has without calling
Contact her bank right away to report it
questions.explain: Reporting an unknown charge quickly helps the bank stop fraud and protect your money. Fast action also makes it easier to get the charge reviewed.

questions.q: A bank offers a checking account with a 12 dollar monthly fee that is waived if your balance stays above 500 dollars. Your balance is 620 dollars all month. How much fee do you pay?
questions.explain: Your balance stayed above 500 dollars, so the fee is waived and you pay 0 dollars. Always read the rules for avoiding account fees.

questions.q: What is direct deposit?
options: Cash you hand to a bank teller
Your pay is sent electronically straight into your bank account
A loan your employer gives you
A fee for using direct mail
questions.explain: Direct deposit moves your paycheck into your account automatically on payday. It is faster and safer than carrying a paper check.

questions.explain: A savings account keeps the money safe, easy to reach, and earning a little interest.
options: In a checking account you spend from
questions.q: Where is the best place to keep an emergency fund?
A job pays $30,000 per year. About how much is that per month?

questions.explain: Moving money into savings first, before spending, makes saving a habit instead of an afterthought.
options: Pay your friends before your bills
Spend your whole paycheck, then save
Save money before you spend on anything else
questions.q: What does 'pay yourself first' mean?

subject: Financial Literacy
title: Percentages & Interest
Credit and Credit Scores
subject: Financial Literacy
description: Understand what credit is, how credit scores are built, and how on-time payments and low balances protect your future borrowing.

questions.q: What does it mean to buy something on credit?
options: You pay cash before you get it
You get it now and pay for it later
You trade an item for it
questions.explain: Credit lets you receive goods or money now with a promise to pay later. That promise usually comes with rules and sometimes interest.

questions.q: What is a credit score?
options: The amount of cash in your wallet
How many credit cards you own
A number that shows how reliably you have handled borrowing and repayment
questions.explain: Lenders use credit scores to judge repayment risk. Paying on time and keeping balances low helps build a strong score.

questions.q: Which action is most likely to help your credit score over time?
options: Opening ten cards in one week
Ignoring a bill you cannot pay
Using all of your credit limit each month
Paying every bill on time, every time
questions.explain: Payment history is the biggest part of most credit scores. On-time payments month after month show you are reliable.

questions.q: What is a credit limit?
options: The most you are allowed to charge on a credit card
The least you must spend each month
A fee for using a card
questions.explain: Your credit limit is the ceiling on what you can borrow on that card. Staying well below it is healthier for your score.

questions.q: Jordan has a 1,000 dollar credit limit and charges 200 dollars. What percent of the limit did Jordan use?
questions.explain: Divide 200 by 1,000 to get 0.20, which is 20 percent. Keeping usage low, often under 30 percent, is good for your score.

questions.q: Why do landlords and lenders check credit reports?
options: To check your grades in school
To see how you have handled money and debts in the past
To count your social media followers
questions.explain: A credit report shows your borrowing and payment history. Lenders and landlords use it to predict whether you will pay reliably.

questions.q: What happens if you only pay the minimum amount due on a credit card each month?
options: The rest of the balance is forgiven
The card company stops charging interest
The leftover balance keeps growing interest, so the purchase costs much more
questions.explain: Paying only the minimum leaves a balance that accrues interest. Paying in full each month avoids interest charges entirely.

questions.q: Alex missed a payment and it is now 10 days late. What is the smartest next step?
options: Pay it as soon as possible and call the company if a fee was added
Wait a full year to pay it
Open a new card and forget the old one
questions.explain: Paying quickly limits extra fees and damage to your record. Calling politely can sometimes get a first late fee removed.

questions.q: Which of these would most likely hurt a credit score?
options: Missing payments and maxing out a card
questions.explain: Late payments and maxed-out cards signal risk to lenders. Checking your own report never hurts your score.

questions.q: Sam pays a 450 dollar credit card balance in full before the due date and the card charges no interest on purchases paid in full. How much interest does Sam pay?
questions.explain: Paying the full statement balance by the due date means no interest is charged. That is the cheapest way to use a credit card.

title: Debt and Borrowing Smart
subject: Financial Literacy
description: Learn how loans, interest, and repayment plans work, and how to tell helpful borrowing from debt that traps you.

questions.q: What is a loan principal?
options: The original amount of money you borrowed
questions.explain: The principal is the amount borrowed before interest is added. Your payments reduce the principal over time.

questions.q: What is interest on a loan?
options: A free bonus from the lender
The money you get back at the end
The extra cost you pay for borrowing money
questions.explain: Interest is the price of borrowing, usually a percent of the principal. Higher rates and longer terms mean you pay more overall.

questions.q: You borrow 500 dollars at 10 percent simple interest for 1 year. How much interest will you pay?
questions.explain: Multiply 500 by 0.10 by 1 year to get 50 dollars of interest. The total repaid would be 550 dollars.

questions.q: What does APR stand for?
questions.explain: APR is the yearly cost of borrowing shown as a percent. Comparing APRs helps you find the cheaper loan.

questions.q: Which loan will usually cost less in total interest?
options: A loan with a higher APR
A loan where you skip payments
A loan repaid in 2 years instead of 5 years at the same rate
A bigger loan for the same item
questions.explain: Shorter repayment means fewer months of interest adding up. The monthly payment is higher, but the total cost is lower.

questions.q: What is collateral?
options: The first payment on a loan
Something valuable a lender can take if you do not repay a loan
questions.explain: Secured loans use collateral, such as a car for an auto loan. If you stop paying, the lender can claim the collateral.

questions.q: Priya owes 300 dollars on one card at 24 percent APR and 300 dollars on another at 12 percent APR. If she has extra money, paying which card first saves the most interest?
options: Neither; she should buy something instead
questions.explain: Attacking the highest rate first, called the avalanche method, cuts the fastest-growing interest. Keep paying minimums on both cards meanwhile.

questions.q: What is a payday loan risk?
options: It always has the lowest rate
Very high fees that can trap borrowers in a cycle of new loans
questions.explain: Payday loans charge fees that equal extremely high annual rates. Many borrowers roll them over and end up owing far more than they borrowed.

questions.q: You take a loan with monthly payments of 85 dollars for 12 months on a 900 dollar item. How much do you pay in total?
questions.explain: Multiply 85 by 12 to get 1,020 dollars total. That is 120 dollars more than the item price, which is the cost of borrowing.

questions.q: What is the best reason to borrow money?
options: To buy every new gadget on release day
To lend it to a stranger online
Because a store says today only
For something valuable you can afford to repay, like education or a needed car
questions.explain: Smart borrowing funds lasting value and fits your budget with room to spare. If the payments strain your budget, the loan is too big.

title: Taxes Made Simple
subject: Financial Literacy
description: Find out where taxes come from, what a paycheck deduction means, and what happens each year when people file a tax return.

questions.q: What is income tax?
options: A tip you leave at restaurants
Interest a savings account pays you
Money paid to the government based on what you earn
questions.explain: Income tax is a share of your earnings paid to federal, state, and sometimes local governments. It funds public services.

questions.q: Which public services are paid for with tax money?
questions.explain: Taxes fund services everyone shares, from roads and schools to emergency services. That is why paying taxes is a civic duty.

questions.q: What is a sales tax?
options: A discount for shopping on weekends
An extra percent added to the price of many things you buy
questions.explain: Sales tax is added at checkout in most states and varies by place. It is calculated as a percent of the purchase price.

questions.q: A jacket costs 50 dollars and sales tax is 8 percent. How much tax do you pay?
questions.explain: Multiply 50 by 0.08 to get 4 dollars of tax. The total at checkout would be 54 dollars.

questions.q: What does a W-2 form show?
options: Your bank account number for loans
A list of items you bought
How much you earned and how much tax was already withheld that year
questions.explain: Employers send a W-2 each January summarizing wages and withholding. You use it to file your tax return.

questions.q: What does it mean when tax is withheld from a paycheck?
options: Your employer sends part of your pay to the government before you receive it
Your employer keeps the money as a bonus
You never have to file taxes
questions.explain: Withholding spreads your tax payments across the year. At filing time you settle up for any difference.

questions.q: What is a tax refund?
options: Money back when you paid more tax during the year than you owed
questions.explain: If withholding was more than your actual tax, the government returns the extra as a refund. It is your own money coming back, not a prize.

questions.q: Leo earned 12,000 dollars and had 900 dollars withheld. His actual tax is 750 dollars. How much is his refund?
questions.explain: Subtract the tax owed from what was withheld: 900 minus 750 equals a 150 dollar refund. Over-withholding means a smaller paycheck during the year.

questions.q: What is the usual federal tax filing deadline in the United States?
questions.explain: Federal tax returns are usually due in mid-April, often April 15. Filing on time avoids late penalties.

questions.q: Why should you keep pay stubs and tax forms in a safe place?
options: You may need them to prove income or fix a filing mistake
They are worth money at stores
Banks require them for every purchase
questions.explain: Good records prove what you earned and paid if questions come up. Keep tax documents for at least three years.
